mainTopic: Which sins bring the court's bull and the אשם תלוי: none for Temple impurity, yes for נדה; the word-links that prove it; and whether the king brings the sliding-scale offering.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an older search: a second verse, 'from the day that ה׳ commanded,' is offered to show the communal sin-offering is about עבודה זרה. That proof fails because ten מצוות were given at מרה, so the גמרא returns to its first source. A new משנה then teaches that the court's bull and the individual's אשם תלוי do not apply to the Temple-impurity laws, but they do apply to the laws of נדה. רב יצחק בר אבדימי links the words ואשם and ואשמו to show that both offerings come only for sins that bring a fixed חטאת. After challenges from other word forms and from the טומאת מקדש section, רב פפא and then רב נחמן בר יצחק strengthen the link by adding more shared phrases. A second משנה says the court is not liable for the three sliding-scale sins, and רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא argue about whether the king is exempt. עולא's source for רבי יוסי הגלילי is challenged, and the גמרא begins a new source from רבי ירמיה that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A second attempt: idol worship was the first מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another verse, 'from the day that ה׳ commanded,' and argues that the first מצוה ever given was עבודה זרה. So the communal sin-offering must be about עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'from the day that the Lord commanded and onward throughout your generations.' Which מצוה was said first of all? It must be idol worship.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is offering a new proof, from a different verse, that the passage about the community's sin-offering is talking about עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse points back to 'the day ה׳ commanded,' which means the very first commandment. The proof assumes the first commandment was the ban on idol worship, the opening of the עשרת הדברות. If that holds, the verse is pointing at עבודה זרה.

keyTerms.meaning: you must say, it must be

phrases.english: "From the day that the Lord commanded
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:23

phrases.english: and onward throughout your generations."
Which is the מצוה
that was said at the very beginning?
You must say: this is idol worship.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמִן הַיּוֹם אֲשֶׁר צִוָּה ה׳ וָהָלְאָה לְדוֹרוֹתֵיכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative source, from the earlier part of the sugya, that the communal offering is about עבודה זרה.
steps.raayaObject: That the communal sin-offering passage is about עבודה זרה
steps.raayaSupportSource: במדבר 15:23, 'from the day that ה׳ commanded,' read as pointing to the first מצוה

steps.title: But מצוות were already given at מרה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: we know ten מצוות were given at מרה, before סיני. So idol worship was not the first מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the Master taught that Israel was commanded ten מצוות at מרה, as it says: 'If you will listen to the voice of the Lord your God.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the proof from Step 1 by showing that idol worship was not really the first מצוה ever given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 depended on idol worship being the first commandment. The teaching about מרה shows other מצוות came earlier, right after leaving מצרים. With that assumption gone, the verse 'from the day ה׳ commanded' no longer points only to עבודה זרה.

keyTerms.meaning: but didn't the Master say? (an objection from a known teaching)
Marah, a stop in the desert before Mount Sinai

phrases.english: But didn't the Master say:
Israel was commanded ten מצוות at Marah
(as it is written:
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets here.

phrases.english: "If you will surely listen
to the voice of the Lord your God")?
phrases.notes: שמות 15:26

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אָמַר מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption behind Step 1's proof.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that עבודה זרה was the first מצוה given
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Ten מצוות were given at מרה, before סיני, so idol worship cannot be 'the first' מצוה.

steps.title: Back to the original answer
steps.stepSummary: The second proof fails, so the גמרא returns to the source it gave at first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is clear as we answered at the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the new proof and says the first explanation it gave is the right one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the objection from מרה, the verse 'from the day ה׳ commanded' cannot prove the point. The earlier answer still stands, so the conclusion that the communal offering is about עבודה זרה stays in place, just not from this verse.
steps.whatToRemember: The ruling stays the same (the communal offering is about עבודה זרה). Only the second proof was dropped, and the גמרא relies on its first source.

phrases.english: Rather, it is clear
as we answered at the start.
phrases.notes: This means the source the גמרא gave earlier, before this second try.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מְחַוַּורְתָּא כִדְשַׁנִּינַן מֵעִיקָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts Step 2's objection and goes back to the first source.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The alternative proof is rejected. The source for עבודה זרה remains the one the גמרא gave first.

steps.title: No offerings for Temple-impurity laws
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that for the positive מצוה or the prohibition about the מקדש, the court brings no communal bull and an individual brings no אשם תלוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The court is not liable for a positive מצוה or a prohibition relating to the Temple. And one does not bring a provisional guilt-offering for a positive מצוה or a prohibition relating to the Temple.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that wrongly permitting or doing Temple-impurity sins does not bring the usual offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These laws are about the מקדש and its holy food: impure people must be sent out, and an impure person may not enter. Even so, the court brings no bull for ruling wrongly about them, and someone unsure if he sinned brings no אשם תלוי.

keyTerms.meaning: a positive מצוה, something you must do
a prohibition, something you must not do
provisional guilt-offering, brought when unsure whether one sinned

steps.confusionAlert: 'שבמקדש' does not mean every Temple law. Here it means the laws of being in the מקדש, or eating its holy food, while impure.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
They are not liable for a positive מצוה
phrases.notes: 'They' is the court, which would otherwise bring a bull for a mistaken ruling.

phrases.english: or for a prohibition relating to the Temple,
phrases.notes: This means coming into the מקדש, or eating its holy food, while impure.

phrases.english: and one does not bring a provisional guilt-offering

phrases.aramaic: עַל עֲשֵׂה וְעַל לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁבַּמִּקְדָּשׁ.
phrases.english: for a positive מצוה or a prohibition relating to the Temple.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין חַיָּיבִין עַל עֲשֵׂה וְעַל לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁבַּמִּקְדָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No communal bull and no אשם תלוי for the Temple-impurity laws.

steps.title: But offerings are brought for the laws of נדה
steps.stepSummary: In contrast, for the positive מצוה and prohibition about נדה, the court is liable and an individual brings an אשם תלוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: But they are liable for a positive מצוה or a prohibition relating to a menstruating woman, and one brings a provisional guilt-offering for a positive מצוה or a prohibition relating to a menstruating woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the opposite case: for the laws of נדה, the normal offerings do apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses the same wording as before ('positive מצוה and prohibition'), so the contrast is sharp. The מקדש laws are left out, while the נדה laws are included in both the court's bull and the individual's אשם תלוי.

keyTerms.meaning: a woman in her menstrual state, forbidden for relations

phrases.english: But they are liable for a positive מצוה
or a prohibition relating to a menstruating woman,
and one brings a provisional guilt-offering

phrases.aramaic: עַל עֲשֵׂה וְעַל לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁבַּנִּדָּה.
phrases.english: for a positive מצוה or a prohibition relating to a menstruating woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל חַיָּיבִין עַל עֲשֵׂה וְעַל לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁבַּנִּדָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the contrasting case to Step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The communal bull and the אשם תלוי do apply to the נדה laws.

steps.title: What are the two מצוות of נדה?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה defines the positive מצוה (separate from her) and the prohibition (do not have relations with her).
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the positive מצוה relating to a menstruating woman? Separate from her. And the prohibition? Do not have relations with a menstruating woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains exactly which two נדה מצוות it meant in Step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prohibition covers starting relations with a woman who is a נדה. The positive מצוה covers a case where she becomes a נדה during relations, so the man must separate from her. The משנה asks the question itself and answers it right away.

keyTerms.meaning: do not come (do not have relations)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's contrast: the Temple-impurity laws bring no offerings. The נדה laws (separating from her, and not having relations with her) bring both the communal bull and the אשם תלוי.

phrases.english: What is the positive מצוה relating to a menstruating woman?
Separate from the menstruating woman.
And the prohibition?
Do not have relations with a menstruating woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיזוֹ הִיא מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה שֶׁבַּנִּדָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the terms used in Step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The positive מצוה is to separate from a נדה. The prohibition is not to have relations with a נדה.

steps.title: Where do we learn the Temple exemption?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that the community brings no offering at all for Temple-impurity laws, and that an individual also brings no אשם תלוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where are these matters derived, that the community is not liable for any offering at all, and an individual is also not liable to bring a provisional guilt-offering?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its discussion of the משנה by asking for the source of the Temple exemption. It is setting up the next move, where it will bring that source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For טומאת מקדש, the individual does not bring the regular fixed חטאת, so the court's bull does not apply. The גמרא asks where we learn that the community brings no offering of any kind here. It also asks why the individual does not even bring an אשם תלוי.

keyTerms.meaning: גמרא, the discussion of the משנה
from where are these things derived?

phrases.english: GEMARA:
From where are these matters derived
that the community is not liable
for any offering at all,
and that an individual is also not liable to bring a provisional guilt-offering?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the scriptural source of Step 4's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that the community brings no offering, and the individual no אשם תלוי, for Temple-impurity laws.

steps.title: The shared word ואשם ties the community to a fixed sin-offering
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר אבדימי makes a גזירה שוה between ואשם (individual) and ואשמו (community). The community, like the individual, is only liable where there is a fixed חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר אבדימי said: 'and he is guilty' is written about a sin-offering and about a provisional guilt-offering, and 'and they are guilty' is written about the community. Just as 'and he is guilty' for an individual is about a fixed sin-offering, so too 'and they are guilty' for the community is about a fixed sin-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 7 with a word-link, a גזירה שוה. It starts with the community's part of the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the individual, the word ואשם appears with sins that bring a fixed חטאת. Because the community's פסוק uses the same root (ואשמו), the community is also limited to sins that bring a fixed חטאת. טומאת מקדש brings a sliding-scale offering, not a fixed one, so the community brings no bull for it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And he is guilty': the key word of the link
'And they are guilty': the same word in plural, said about the community
A fixed sin-offering: the same animal no matter how rich or poor the person is
A 'hanging' guilt-offering, brought when a person is unsure whether he sinned

steps.confusionAlert: Here ואשם does not mean an אשם offering. It is a verb that means 'he is guilty'. It shows up even in the פסוק of a חטאת.

phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Avdimi said:
'And he is guilty' is said about a sin-offering and about a provisional guilt-offering,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:27 and ויקרא 5:17.

phrases.english: and 'and they are guilty' is said about the community.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:13

phrases.english: Just as 'and he is guilty' by an individual is about a fixed sin-offering,
so too 'and they are guilty' by the community is about a fixed sin-offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר אַבְדִּימִי: נֶאֱמַר ״וְאָשֵׁם״ בְּחַטָּאת וּבְאָשָׁם תָּלוּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה from ואשם and ואשמו limits the community's offering to sins that bring a fixed חטאת.

steps.title: The same link limits the אשם תלוי
steps.stepSummary: The link is carried one step further. The אשם תלוי also comes only when a person is unsure about a sin that brings a fixed חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And just as the community is about a fixed sin-offering, so too a provisional guilt-offering comes only for a doubt about a fixed sin-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer to step 7. It covers the second part of the question: why an individual brings no אשם תלוי for טומאת מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אשם תלוי shares the word ואשם with the community, which is now limited to a fixed חטאת. So the אשם תלוי is also limited to doubts about fixed-חטאת sins. A doubt about טומאת מקדש would only lead to a sliding-scale offering, so no אשם תלוי is brought for it.
steps.whatToRemember: One word-link answers both halves of the question in step 7. Both the community bull and the אשם תלוי are tied to a fixed חטאת, so neither applies to טומאת מקדש.

phrases.english: And just as the community is about a fixed sin-offering,
so too the provisional guilt-offering also

phrases.aramaic: אֵין בָּא אֶלָּא עַל סְפֵק חַטָּאת קְבוּעָה.
phrases.english: comes only for a doubt about a fixed sin-offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה צִבּוּר בְּחַטָּאת קְבוּעָה, אַף אָשָׁם תָּלוּי נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the link from step 8 to the אשם תלוי.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The אשם תלוי is brought only for a doubt about a sin that brings a fixed חטאת.

steps.title: The sliding-scale offering also uses a guilt-word
steps.stepSummary: The Sages object that the קרבן עולה ויורד also has a form of the word: יאשם. So why not link the community to that offering instead?
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: If so, the sliding-scale offering too has this word, for it is written: 'And it shall be when he is guilty of one of these.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the link. A related word also appears in the section of the sliding-scale offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a shared guilt-word is enough to link פסוקים, the community could just as well be linked to the קרבן עולה ויורד. Then the result would be the opposite: the community would be liable for טומאת מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: A sliding-scale offering: its size goes up or down according to the person's wealth
'He shall be guilty': a different form of the same root

phrases.english: They say: If so,
the sliding-scale offering also has it,

phrases.aramaic: הָא כְּתִיב: ״וְהָיָה כִּי יֶאְשַׁם לְאַחַת מֵאֵלֶּה״!
phrases.english: for it is written: 'And it shall be when he is guilty of one of these'!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:5

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: אִי הָכִי, קׇרְבָּן עוֹלֶה וְיוֹרֵד נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the link from steps 8-9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יצחק בר אבדימי's גזירה שוה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A competing פסוק with a similar word could link the community to the sliding-scale offering instead.

steps.title: Only close word-forms are linked
steps.stepSummary: The answer: ואשמו can be learned from ואשם, but ואשם is not learned from יאשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn 'they are guilty' from 'he is guilty,' but we do not learn 'he is guilty' from 'he shall be guilty.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the link by pointing to the exact form of each word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ואשם and ואשמו have the same form, one singular and one plural. יאשם is a different form of the word. So the link holds only with the matching form.

keyTerms.meaning: We learn one case from another

phrases.english: We learn 'they are guilty' from 'he is guilty,'
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in round brackets, which point the other way; the words in square brackets are the corrected wording.

phrases.english: but we do not learn 'he is guilty' from 'he shall be guilty.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּנִין ״אָשֵׁמוּ״ מִן ״אָשֵׁם״, וְאֵין דָּנִין ״אָשֵׁם״ מִן ״יֶאְשַׁם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any form of the root could make a link.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the closely matching form ואשם/ואשמו makes the link.

steps.title: Even different words can be linked
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the word-form distinction. דבי רבי ישמעאל linked two completely different words, ושב and ובא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what difference does it make? But the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: 'And the priest shall return' and 'And the priest shall come': this returning is like this coming!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer in step 11 using a teaching from the laws of a house with צרעת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דבי רבי ישמעאל made a גזירה שוה between 'return' and 'come', two different words. If different words can be linked, two forms of the same root surely can. So יאשם should be able to link too.

phrases.english: And what difference does it make?
But the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
'And the priest shall return,' 'and the priest shall come':
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:39 and 14:44, in the laws of a house with צרעת.

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ הִיא שִׁיבָה, זוֹ הִיא בִּיאָה!
phrases.english: this is returning, this is coming!
phrases.notes: He means the two words count as the same for learning one case from the other.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי נָפְקָא מִינַּהּ? וְהָא תָּנֵי דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The distinction between ואשם and יאשם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If even different words can be linked, different forms of one word surely can.

steps.title: טומאת מקדש itself says ואשם
steps.stepSummary: A further challenge: the section on טומאת מקדש uses the exact word ואשם. So the link should point there.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, let us learn from 'and he is guilty' about the impurity of the Temple and its holy foods, as it is written: 'And he is impure and he is guilty'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second, stronger challenge to רב יצחק בר אבדימי's link.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No word-form distinction can help here, because the word is exactly the same. Linking to this פסוק would tie the community and the אשם תלוי to טומאת מקדש, the opposite of the ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Entering the מקדש or eating holy food while impure

phrases.english: And furthermore: let us learn from 'and he is guilty'
written about the impurity of the Temple and its holy foods,
as it is written: 'And he is impure and he is guilty'!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:2

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד: נֵילַף מִן ״וְאָשֵׁם״ מִטּוּמְאַת מִקְדָּשׁ וְקָדָשָׁיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second challenge alongside step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יצחק בר אבדימי's גזירה שוה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The identical word appears by טומאת מקדש, so the link could point to the sliding-scale offering.

steps.title: A double link: ואשם together with מצות ה׳
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the link rests on two shared phrases, ואשם and מצות ה׳. Those two appear together only in the fixed-offering sections.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: We learn 'and he is guilty' and 'the commandments of the Lord' from 'and he is guilty' and 'the commandments of the Lord.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא saves the link from the challenges of steps 10-13.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אשם תלוי פסוק has both ואשם and מצות ה׳. So do the fixed sin-offering sections. The טומאת מקדש section has ואשם but not מצות ה׳, so the stronger, two-word match points to the fixed offering.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The commandments of the Lord': a second matching phrase

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
We learn 'and he is guilty' and 'the commandments of the Lord'
phrases.notes: These are the words in the אשם תלוי פסוק, ויקרא 5:17.

phrases.english: from 'and he is guilty' and 'the commandments of the Lord.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: דָּנִין ״וְאָשֵׁם״ וּ״מִצְוֹת ה׳״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers steps 12-13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Strengthening the link with a second shared phrase
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The single word ואשם could link to טומאת מקדש.
steps.terutzMaskana: The double match of ואשם with מצות ה׳ links only to the fixed sin-offering.

steps.title: A rival double link: ואשם with ונשא עונו
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר אשי answers with a competing two-word link. The phrases ואשם and נשיאת עון appear by both the אשם תלוי and טומאת מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר אשי said to רב פפא: But let us learn 'and he is guilty' and 'bearing iniquity' from 'and he is guilty' and 'bearing iniquity'!
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי בר אשי challenges רב פפא's answer with a double link of his own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אשם תלוי פסוק also says ונשא עונו. That phrase, together with ואשם, also appears in the section of the sliding-scale offering. So a two-word match pointing to טומאת מקדש exists too, and רב פפא's double link no longer settles the question.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי לְרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Ashi said to Rav Pappa:
But let us learn 'and he is guilty' and 'bearing iniquity'
phrases.notes: These are also in the אשם תלוי פסוק, ויקרא 5:17.

phrases.english: from 'and he is guilty' and 'bearing iniquity'!
phrases.notes: These are in the sliding-scale offering section, ויקרא 5:1-4.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי לְרַב פָּפָּא: וְנֵילַף ״וְאָשֵׁם״ וּנְשִׂיאַת עָוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's answer in step 14.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An equally strong two-word match ties the אשם תלוי to the sliding-scale offering of טומאת מקדש.

steps.title: The final link: two shared phrases point only to the fixed חטאת
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says the אשם תלוי is linked to the fixed חטאת through the pair of phrases ואשם and מצות ה׳ אשר לא תעשינה. The sliding-scale cases cannot argue against this, because they do not contain that pair.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב נחמן בר יצחק says: we learn 'and he is guilty' and 'the commandments of ה׳ that shall not be done' in the אשם תלוי from the same two phrases in the fixed חטאת. The cases of שמיעת קול, ביטוי שפתים and טומאת מקדש וקדשיו do not prove otherwise, because those two phrases are not written about them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the question of which section the אשם תלוי is linked to. רב נחמן בר יצחק says the pair of phrases only matches the fixed חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא shows that רב פפא's two-term link (ואשם with מצות ה׳) could not stand against רב שימי בר אשי's equally strong two-term link (ואשם with נשיאת עון). רב נחמן בר יצחק adds a third shared element, אשר לא תעשינה. ואשם, מצות ה׳ and אשר לא תעשינה all appear in both the אשם תלוי and the fixed חטאת, so this match is stronger than the rival pair. The sliding-scale cases do not have this full set of words, so they cannot be used to break the link.

keyTerms.meaning: We learn one case from another
And let this case not prove otherwise
A witness who falsely swears he knows no testimony
A false oath about something said with the lips
Entering the מקדש or eating holy food while טמא

steps.whatToRemember: The אשם תלוי is linked to the fixed חטאת, and not to the sliding-scale offering, because only those two sections share both ואשם and מצות ה׳ אשר לא תעשינה.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak says:
We learn "and he is guilty"
and "the commandments of ה׳ that shall not be done"
phrases.notes: These two phrases are from the אשם תלוי section, ויקרא 5:17.

phrases.aramaic: מִ״וְאָשֵׁם וּמִצְוֹת ה׳ אֲשֶׁר לֹא תֵעָשֶׂינָה״.
phrases.english: from "and he is guilty" and "the commandments of ה׳ that shall not be done".
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:27, the section of the fixed חטאת.

phrases.english: And do not let hearing of a voice prove otherwise
or an utterance of the lips
or defiling the Temple and its holy foods,
since it is not said about them "and he is guilty"
and "the commandments of ה׳ that shall not be done".

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב שימי בר אשי's competing two-word link by setting out the pair that fits only the fixed חטאת.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Refined word-link (two phrases that must appear together)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ואשם / נשיאת עון pair could link the אשם תלוי to טומאת מקדש.
steps.terutzMaskana: Adding אשר לא תעשינה makes the match with the fixed חטאת stronger than רב שימי בר אשי's ואשם / נשיאת עון pair. The sliding-scale cases lack this full set of words and cannot disprove the link.

steps.title: משנה: no liability for the sliding-scale cases, and the king is like the court
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that the court is not liable for a mistaken ruling about שמיעת קול, ביטוי שפתים, or טומאת מקדש וקדשיו. רבי יוסי הגלילי says the king is also exempt in these.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: They are not liable for שמיעת קול, ביטוי שפתים, or טומאת מקדש וקדשיו. And the king is the same as them. These are the words of רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It says that the court's special offering does not apply to the three sins that bring a sliding-scale offering, and רבי יוסי הגלילי puts the king in the same category.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These three sins bring a קרבן עולה ויורד, an offering whose cost changes with the sinner's wealth. The משנה says the court does not bring an offering for a mistaken ruling about them. רבי יוסי הגלילי adds that the king does not bring an offering for them either.

keyTerms.meaning: Sliding-scale offering, whose cost depends on the sinner's means

phrases.english: MISHNA:
They are not liable for hearing of a voice,
phrases.notes: 'They' means the court that gave a mistaken ruling.

phrases.english: or for an utterance of the lips,
or for defiling the Temple and its holy foods.
And the king is the same as them,
these are the words of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין חַיָּיבִין עַל שְׁמִיעַת קוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The court is exempt for the three sliding-scale sins. According to רבי יוסי הגלילי, the king is exempt too.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the king is liable in all except שמיעת קול
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא disagrees. The king is liable in all three cases except שמיעת קול, because a king does not judge, is not judged, does not testify, and is not testified against.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: the king is liable in all of them except שמיעת קול, because the king does not judge and is not judged, does not testify and is not testified against.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא gives the other side of the מחלוקת. The king brings the sliding-scale offering for everything except the false oath about testimony.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמיעת קול is a false oath by someone asked to testify. A king never testifies, so he can never be in that situation. His exemption comes from his position as king, not from a rule that the offering does not apply to him.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not judge and is not judged

steps.confusionAlert: רבי עקיבא does not say the sliding-scale offering does not apply to the king. The king is exempt from שמיעת קול only because a king never serves as a witness.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
The king is liable in all of them
except for hearing of a voice,
because the king does not judge
and others do not judge him
[he does not testify and others do not testify about him].
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are part of the corrected wording; not every version has them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: הַנָּשִׂיא חַיָּיב בְּכוּלָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי יוסי הגלילי about the king.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The king is liable in all the sliding-scale cases except שמיעת קול, because he never testifies.

steps.title: What is רבי יוסי הגלילי's reason?
steps.stepSummary: עולא asks what source supports רבי יוסי הגלילי's ruling that the king is exempt in all three cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: עולא said: What is the reason of רבי יוסי הגלילי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by asking why רבי יוסי הגלילי exempts the king. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא gave a reason for exempting the king only from שמיעת קול. The question is why רבי יוסי הגלילי exempts the king from the other two cases as well.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Ulla said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה by asking for רבי יוסי הגלילי's source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural basis for exempting the king from all the sliding-scale cases.

steps.title: 'One of these': whoever can be liable in each is liable in all
steps.stepSummary: עולא answers from the פסוק 'when he is guilty in one of these.' Only someone who can be liable in every one of the cases is liable at all. The king can never be liable for שמיעת קול, so he is exempt from all three.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And it shall be when he is guilty in one of these.' Whoever can become liable in each one becomes liable in all of them. Whoever cannot become liable in each one does not become liable in any of them.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא explains רבי יוסי הגלילי's reason. He reads 'one of these' to mean the cases form a package, all or nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The king can never be liable for שמיעת קול, because he never testifies. Since he fails one case, the package rule exempts him from the other two as well. This explains why רבי יוסי הגלילי exempts the king completely.
steps.whyThisMatters: This all-or-nothing rule is the whole basis for רבי יוסי הגלילי's view, and the next step challenges it.

phrases.english: The verse says:
"And it shall be when he is guilty in one of these",
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:5

phrases.english: whoever becomes liable in each one
becomes liable in all of them,
and whoever does not become liable in each one
does not become liable in any of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: וְהָיָה כִי יֶאְשַׁם לְאַחַת מֵאֵלֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers עולא's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'לאחת מאלה' makes the sliding-scale cases all-or-nothing. The king fails שמיעת קול, so he is exempt from all of them.

steps.title: Maybe 'one of these' means any single one is enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges עולא's reading. Maybe the פסוק means that a person is liable for any single case he can commit, even if he cannot be liable in all of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say instead: he becomes liable in one of them, even though he is not liable in all of them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on עולא's reading. It offers the opposite way to read 'one of these.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'one of these' could just as easily mean that each case stands alone. On that reading, the king would bring the offering for the cases he can commit, even though he cannot commit שמיעת קול. That reading is what רבי עקיבא holds, so עולא's proof no longer seems to force רבי יוסי הגלילי's view.

phrases.english: But say instead:
he becomes liable in one of them,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין מִתְחַיֵּיב בְּכוּלָּן!
phrases.english: even though he does not become liable in all of them!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא: מִתְחַיֵּיב בְּאַחַת מֵהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges עולא's reading of the פסוק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The phrase could mean that liability for any single case is enough, so the king would be liable for the cases he can commit.

steps.title: A new source for רבי יוסי הגלילי begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sets aside עולא's reading and starts to offer a different source for רבי יוסי הגלילי, from a ברייתא quoting רבי ירמיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the reason for רבי יוסי הגלילי's opinion comes from here, as a ברייתא teaches: רבי ירמיה used to say: It says...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is giving up on עולא's explanation and is setting up a new answer. It opens a ברייתא where רבי ירמיה is about to quote a פסוק, and the quote comes in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא tells us the challenge in Step 21 worked, so עולא's proof from 'one of these' is dropped. The גמרא now says the real reason for רבי יוסי הגלילי comes from a different teaching, in the name of רבי ירמיה. We have not yet heard what the new proof is, only where it comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals that the earlier explanation is being dropped for a new one.
The reason or source behind an opinion
From here. The source is about to be pointed out.
It is stated. It introduces a quote from a פסוק.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי יוסי הגלילי's ruling was rejected. Only עולא's way of proving it was dropped. The ruling stays, and the גמרא is just looking for a better source.

phrases.english: Rather, the reason of רבי יוסי הגלילי
phrases.notes: 'Rather' means the גמרא is giving up on עולא's proof from Step 20 because of the challenge in Step 21.

phrases.english: is from here, as it is taught in a ברייתא:
רבי ירמיה would say: It is stated:

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 21 knocked down עולא's reading, this step sets it aside and opens a new source for the same ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the source for רבי יוסי הגלילי's ruling that the king is exempt in all three cases? (asked in Step 19)
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is a ברייתא in which רבי ירמיה quotes a פסוק. The details come in the next line.
